summary: Iter 66 backend tested end-to-end: state-filings CSV adapter (MI/TX/FL/CA/NY), DNS/MX email verifier, heuristic enrichment, autopilot cycle wiring, dashboard counters, live-feed, deliverability, daily-cap, unsubscribe, and regression of /dashboard /state /prospects/list. 17/17 pytest cases green. The CSV → state_filings → enrichment → outbound_prospects pipeline works correctly (records_found=20, added=20 first run, dedup=20 on re-upload, enrichment payloads complete, recent business-domain MX-verified emails are forwarded). TEST 14 (Last Cycle no longer 0/0/0) verified — non-zero counts achievable when unique businesses are uploaded; on steady-state runs the cycle correctly reports reasons=['daily_cap_reached','nothing_to_score'] which is design-correct.

minor.issue: deliverability panel returns 'risk' (not 'risk_level') and 'sent' (not 'sent_today') — contract mismatch with iter-66 spec. Frontend likely already adapted; rename for consistency.

When a CSV has multiple rows sharing the same email (e.g. info@cnn.com), only the first row is forwarded into outbound_prospects (subsequent rows hit the email-uniqueness dedup). Documented for op clarity — not a bug, but enrichment for verified rows should arguably synthesize per-row aliases or per-row contact_name to preserve all 5 leads.

records_forwarded in run record can lag the cumulative state_filings.forwarded count when the same verified email is shared across rows of one upload (1 forwarded vs 5 verified). Operator-facing metric — minor confusion only.

action_items: Optional: rename deliverability.risk → risk_level and deliverability.sent → sent_today to match the iter-66 spec contract and downstream UI expectations.

Optional: when a CSV contains multiple rows with the same verified email, decide whether to (a) keep first-only (current), (b) merge into one prospect, or (c) skip duplicate email rows at parse time so the run summary 'forwarded' count matches operator expectations.

Optional: surface 'reasons' from last_autopilot_run.result on the dashboard UI so 'Last Cycle 0/0/0' is explained ('daily cap reached' / 'nothing new to score') instead of looking like a broken engine.
critical_code_review_comments: outbound.py is 2994 lines — beyond the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into modules: outbound_dashboard.py, outbound_engine.py, outbound_replies.py, outbound_sends.py, outbound_unsubscribe.py.

state_business_filings.py uses socket.gethostbyname() as a stand-in for MX lookup. Sufficient for now, but flag: domains with MX-only (no A) won't resolve — currently treated as invalid. Acceptable trade-off given zero-deps requirement; document in module docstring (already done).

ingest_filings forwards on first verified email and silently dedups subsequent rows with the same email — operator-visible metric ('forwarded') drifts from 'verified' count. Consider counting 'skipped_duplicate_email_in_outbound' as its own bucket.
_deliverability_stats sets risk='high' at the threshold but never re-aggregates on demand from the dashboard — fine for now (called per request), but watch for N+1 if dashboard QPS grows.
test_credentials: Founder master key 'jeffrey-2026-bodyiq-founder-master' exchanged via POST /api/ops/founder-access — works.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run inserts 20 fresh state_filings docs (5 verified-MX info{0..4}@cnn.com, 5 bogus invalid, 10 no-email) under MI with TEST_VBiz/BBiz/NBiz_<uuid>_* business names so future runs don't collide via dedup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Server clock is set to May 2026 (forward). Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) for filing_date — DO NOT hardcode 2025-Q4 dates (they fall outside the 30-day lookback). CSV uploads MUST use a non-session requests.post call so the JSON content-type header isn't applied to the multipart body. Email-send is mocked (no RESEND_API_KEY); IMAP is mocked (imap_not_configured). When you re-run the test file, the existing 142 prospects + daily-cap-19 may cause that single autopilot cycle to no-op — that's OK, the test already softens TEST 14 by checking autopilot-history for any prior non-zero cycle.
rca_of_the_issue: No production bugs found. Two test-author traps to avoid: (1) Using business names that don't include a unique slug → re-runs hit dedup → records_added=0 (false TEST-14 fail). Fix: suffix all rows with uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]. (2) Sharing the same email across multiple rows → only one forwards → forwarded count ≠ verified count (looks like a leak but is intentional outbound_prospects email-uniqueness). Fix: per-row unique emails.
